unit.title: Engineering a Small Browser Application
unit.scope: One bounded introductory software-engineering unit; it is not a reconstruction of a Stanford CS142 unit.
unit.audience: A learner with strong algorithms fundamentals and prerequisite-level systems/programming experience who is developing practical software-engineering habits.
prerequisites: Comfort writing and debugging small programs
Ability to reason about arrays, records, ordering, and invariants
Catalog-listed background comparable to CS107 and CS108
learning_objectives: Translate a behavioral specification into a small browser application
Separate pure domain logic from DOM and persistence side effects
Design explicit validation and deterministic state transitions
Write focused automated tests, including boundary and failure cases
Document design choices and verify observable behavior
required_submission: A runnable Algorithm Run Log browser application
Automated tests for domain and persistence behavior
A concise README with execution and verification instructions
Written responses to the comprehension prompts

unit_completion_requires: The worker-harness-controlled validator confirms the submitted files and automated tests
An independent examiner applies examiner_only/RUBRIC.md to observable evidence
All critical safety and execution gates in the rubric are satisfied
later_expansion_conditions: Linked materials are retrieved only by an authorized later job
Retrieved materials are recorded with provenance and availability evidence
Resource links are classified before any resource is promoted to a study unit
Additional units receive independent learner materials and validation

provenance.authorship_note: The catalog identifies the course and links. The kickoff scope, task, questions, and rubric were authored for this learning-factory attempt and are not claimed to be Stanford course content.
